title: Stable homotopy theory of higher categories
summary: Stable homotopy theory is governed by the principle that inverting the operation of forming loop spaces produces representing objects for homology theories. We show that this principle is not specific to topology but reflects an intrinsic structural feature of higher category theory: inverting the operation of forming endomorphism $(\infty,\infty)$-categories leads to a stable homotopy theory of higher categories, in which higher categories play the role of spaces and categorical spectra represent homology theories of higher categories.
